summary: Checks whether a value is a version string.
description: Dot-separated groups of digits, any number of them. A pre-release suffix, a leading `v` and an empty group are all rejected, so `"1.2.3-beta"` does not pass even though SemVer allows it.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is a version string; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
isValidVersion("1"); // => true
isValidVersion("1.2.3"); // => true
isValidVersion("2026.01.15"); // => true
isValidVersion("1.2.3-beta"); // => false
isValidVersion("v1.2"); // => false
isValidVersion("1..2"); // => false
```
